points.description: States that the base case is when the array (sub-array) has size 1 (a single element); size 0 or 1, or size 2 (as in the model answer's alternative), is also acceptable.
points.partial_credit: Half or more of the marks for a vague or partly correct statement, e.g. 'when the array is small enough' or 'when it can't be divided further' without saying size 1, or a size given with a minor error.

points.description: Makes clear the condition applies to the size of the array being sorted in the recursive call (the sub-array is trivially sorted / no further splitting), not to the whole original input.
points.partial_credit: Half if the size is implied but the link to the sub-array or to stopping the recursion is unclear.

rubric.notes: Full marks go to an answer that says the recursion stops when the array or sub-array has one element (size 1; 0/1 or 2 also accepted), in any wording. Part marks go to vague answers such as 'when the array can't be split any more' with no size, or to answers with a minor error. Answers that only describe merging or splitting without a stopping condition get 0.
